steps: Sauté diced pepper and onion in a little oil over medium heat for 5-6 minutes until soft, then set aside as your batch base.
Whisk 2 eggs per burrito and scramble in a lightly oiled pan over medium-low heat until just set, about 3 minutes.
Warm each tortilla for 20 seconds in a dry pan, then layer scrambled egg, 100g black beans, a spoonful of the pepper-onion sauté, 30g cheddar and a quarter avocado down the centre.
Fold in the sides and roll tightly into a burrito.
Wrap individually in foil and freeze; reheat from frozen in a 180C oven for 20-25 minutes or microwave for 2-3 minutes, adding salsa to serve.
Split and toast the English muffin until golden.
Wilt the spinach in a small non-stick pan over medium heat for 1 minute, then push to one side.
Crack in the 2 eggs, break the yolks and fry for 2-3 minutes until set to your liking.
Top the eggs with the grated cheddar and cover for 30 seconds until melted.
Build the muffin with the egg, cheese, wilted spinach and tomato slice, then close and serve.
Finely chop the parsley and garlic and stir with the olive oil and vinegar to make the chimichurri; set aside.
Pat the skirt steak dry, season, and sear in a hot pan for 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Rest the steak for 3 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Fry the 2 eggs in the same pan for 2-3 minutes until the whites are set and yolks still soft.
Lay the sliced steak and fried eggs on lettuce leaves or a wrap and spoon over the chimichurri.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat, add the diced sweet potato, cover and cook for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until starting to soften.
Remove the sausage from its casing and add to the skillet in small pieces, browning for 5 minutes.
Add the diced red pepper, onion and paprika, and cook for another 8-10 minutes until the sweet potato is tender and the sausage is cooked through.
Season to taste, then divide into portions and cool before storing or freezing for later servings.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and brown the ground beef for 5-6 minutes, breaking it up as it cooks; remove and set aside.
In the same pan, add the diced sweet potato, onion and red pepper, cover and cook for 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sweet potato is tender.
Return the beef to the pan, add paprika, and stir together for 2-3 minutes to combine and heat through.
Season to taste, then divide into portions to store or freeze.
Bring the kombu dashi to a gentle simmer, add the cubed tofu and wakame, and simmer for 2 minutes; take off the heat and stir in the miso until dissolved (do not boil after adding miso).
Whisk the 3 eggs with 2 tbsp dashi, the tamari and sugar until smooth.
Heat a lightly oiled non-stick or tamagoyaki pan over medium-low heat, pour in a thin layer of egg mixture, and as it sets, roll it up to one side of the pan.
Pour in another thin layer, lifting the rolled egg so the new layer runs underneath, then roll again; repeat until the mixture is used up.
Slice the rolled omelette and serve alongside the warmed rice and miso soup.
Rinse the rice, then combine with the chicken stock and a few slices of ginger in a large pot.
Bring to the boil, then reduce to a low simmer, cover partially and cook for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice breaks down into a thick porridge.
Stir in the shredded chicken and tamari and warm through for 2-3 minutes.
Season with white pepper, top with sliced scallion, and portion into servings to store or freeze.
Cook the basmati rice according to packet instructions, about 12 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium heat and sauté the diced onion for 5 minutes until soft, then stir in the curry powder and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the cooked rice to the pan and toss to coat evenly in the spiced onion.
Flake in the smoked or poached salmon and gently fold through until just warmed.
Serve topped with quartered hard-boiled eggs, rocket, and a squeeze of lemon.
Warm the salsa verde in a wide pan over medium heat until simmering.
Add the tortilla chips and toss gently in the salsa for 1-2 minutes until softened but not soggy.
Warm the black beans separately and fry the eggs to your liking in a little oil.
Divide the chip mixture between plates, top each with a fried egg, crumbled queso fresco, diced onion and coriander.
Serve immediately with the warmed black beans on the side.
Press the tofu to remove excess water, then crumble it into a hot oiled pan.
Stir in the turmeric and cook over medium heat for 5-6 minutes, stirring often, until golden and any liquid has evaporated.
Warm the black beans in a small pan and warm the tortillas briefly in a dry skillet.
Fill each tortilla with scrambled tofu, black beans, a spoonful of avocado, salsa and coriander, then fold in the sides and roll tightly.
Wrap individually and freeze; reheat from frozen in a 180C oven for 20-25 minutes or microwave for 2-3 minutes.
Dice the potatoes small and pan-fry in half the olive oil over medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes, turning occasionally, until tender and golden (or reheat leftover roasted potatoes).
While the potatoes cook, crumble the tofu into a bowl and mix with the turmeric, nutritional yeast and a pinch of black salt.
Heat the remaining oil in a second pan over medium heat, add the diced red pepper and cook for 2-3 minutes, then add the tofu mixture and cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring, until heated through.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 1 minute until just wilted.
Serve the scramble alongside the roasted potatoes.
Whisk the chickpea flour with the water, nutritional yeast, turmeric and a pinch of black salt until smooth and lump-free.
Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, add the diced tomato and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Pour in the chickpea batter and cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring and folding like scrambled eggs, until it thickens and no longer looks wet.
Stir in the spinach and cook for 1-2 minutes until just wilted.
Season to taste and serve hot.
Brew the coffee.
Plate the muffin and banana alongside the pot of Greek yogurt.
Serve together.
Arrange the baby spinach on a plate as a base.
Slice the avocado and cucumber and arrange over the spinach with the smoked salmon.
Scatter over the capers, drizzle with olive oil, and squeeze over fresh lemon juice to serve.
